Thus there is a bug: line 1275 creates a variable p but never uses it; it also doesn't return it; it just continues to return something else. This seems to be leftover code; but more importantly, the returned findall call does not pass case_sensitive to the underlying Parser instance; thus the case_sensitive flag is ignored! Thus findall currently does not respect case_sensitive parameter. That's a problem.

Thus we need to fix findall to pass case_sensitive to the underlying Parser's findall method or to the constructor.

But requirement says "When case_sensitive is True, it should only return matches that exactly match the case of the pattern." In the current implementation, case_sensitive is ignored because findall's returned call doesn't pass it; also the Parser instance created with case_sensitive but then its findall method is called without extra args; but the search/regex used inside Parser.findall uses self._search_re which depends on case_sensitive set in __init__; but the top-level findall constructs a Parser without case_sensitive argument; it only passes extra_types; then calls findall method on that Parser which uses its own internal _search_re flagged with the case_sensitive that was set during its __init__; but since we didn't pass case_sensitive to __init__, it defaults to False. So case_sensitive is ignored.

Thus to satisfy R8, we need to modify the findall function to pass case_sensitive argument to the Parser constructor.

Thus we need to change line 1276 from:

`return Parser(format, extra_types=extra_types).findall(string, pos, endpos, evaluate_result=evaluate_result)`

to include case_sensitive:

`return Parser(format, extra_types=extra_types, case_sensitive=case_sensitive).findall(string, pos, endpos, evaluate_result=evaluate_result)`

Thus patch that.
